purpose: Train action-conditioned continual world prediction, then falsify its usefulness for actual goal completion with a fixed planner. Not learned general reasoning or the full architecture.
selection: Final fixed128-update models only; no evaluated-world parameter or stopping selection. Development uses separate seeds and reduced budgets.
controls: Within each initialization seed, all training arms receive identical actual uniform-action trajectories and initialization. Equal observations, not compute. Evaluation is closed-loop: agents therefore receive different observations; common maps/schedules/noise seeds and goal-request sequences do not make their evidence identical. Include random, observed-edge BFS and rolling-count model with the same finite Bellman planner.
primary: Whole-world goals completed per512 paid actions, paired by world. Transition NLL and actual accuracy separately. Private full-map argmax coverage is diagnostic only; no controller sees it. A local acquisition criterion is at least11/12 current transition argmaxes correct, with nonrecoveries censored and the known noise probability explicitly retained.
decision: Do not promote the neural mechanism if E2E action completion fails static-plus-TTT/first-order or the simple observed-memory controls at its extra cost. Prediction improvement without action improvement fails the action-usefulness claim. Six-state fixed planner success cannot establish general reasoning, open-ended goal generation, learned compression or recursive self-improvement.
